study_type.note: Claude leads with Experience report, NotebookLM with Case study. The paper says 'We report on the industrial deployment of WhatsCode' and is organised as a chronological narrative (SEIP track).

research_method.claude: Longitudinal industrial deployment report (25 months, 2023–2025) with production metrics (generated/accepted diffs, close rate, verification coverage, precision, weekly active users) and qualitative practitioner feedback; chronological narrative in three eras
research_method.nlm: 25-month longitudinal empirical evaluation of a GenAI tool deployment (case study)
research_method.value: 25-month longitudinal report of a production GenAI deployment (WhatsCode, 2023–2025), narrated in three eras (foundation, agentless, agentic); production metrics such as generated/accepted diffs and close rates per lint type, privacy verification coverage, code quality score, bug-triage precision and weekly active users; no comparison group
research_method.note: Qualitative practitioner feedback (Workplace threads) reported only by Claude.

context.claude: Industry; WhatsApp (Meta), compliance-relevant, polyglot mono-repo (Android, iOS, Web, server; >1M LOC); 3,000+ accepted changes; ~20% weekly active usage; number of engineers not reported
context.nlm: Industry; WhatsApp (Meta), >3 billion users, polyglot monorepo (Android, iOS, Web, Server); 3,000+ accepted diffs; 20% weekly active users
context.value: industry; WhatsApp (Meta) engineering organisation, privacy/compliance-sensitive polyglot codebase (Android, iOS, Web, server); 3,000+ accepted AI-generated code changes, ~20% weekly active usage among WhatsApp engineers (number of engineers not reported)

ai_discussed.note: Domain-specific GenAI/agentic development system (LLMs, RAG, agents) is the object of study.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not specified by either.

data_window.note: Text adds that the foundation era began in July 2023 and diff counts run to September 2025.

cat_productivity.note: Volume of accepted AI-generated changes (feature development assists, refactors, framework adoptions) as business-impact/efficiency output.

cat_quality.note: Code quality score by detected lint issues (45% to 64%), bug-triage precision, incident root-cause identification, test generation.

cat_collaboration.note: Borderline: human-AI collaboration modes (one-click rollout 60%, commandeer-revise 40%) and code review organisation (dedicated vs distributed reviewers) affecting acceptance.

cat_satisfaction.note: No satisfaction measure; Claude cites anecdotal practitioner feedback, NotebookLM labels weekly active users 'Satisfaction' (adoption, not satisfaction).

cat_activity.note: Committed/generated diff counts by platform and category over time.

cat_delivery.note: Both tag diff counts and close rates 'Delivery', but no lead time, deployment or release metric is reported.

cat_devex.note: DevEx framework not used (NotebookLM: DevEx only referenced as a general concept).

cat_survey.note: No survey or interview instrument; Claude mentions only anecdotal feedback threads.

evidence.quote: Over 25 months (2023-2025), WhatsCode evolved from targeted privacy automation to autonomous agentic workflows integrated with end-to-end feature development and DevOps processes.
Based on systematic analysis of 25 months of WhatsCode deployment across WhatsApp's engineering organization, this study addresses two fundamental research questions

We report on the industrial deployment of WhatsCode, a domainspecific AI development system that supports WhatsApp (serving over 3 billion users) and processes millions of lines of code across multiple platforms.
The system achieved significant organic adoption with approximately 20% weekly active usage among WhatsApp engineers

generating over 3,000 accepted code changes with acceptance rates ranging from 9% to 100% across different automation domains. The system committed 692 automated refactor/fix changes, 711 framework adoptions, 141 feature development assists
most notably demonstrated by one Media team's code quality score (measured by detected lint issues) improvement from 45% to 64%.
one-click rollout for high-confidence changes (60% of cases) and commandeer-revise for complex decisions (40%).
83% success rate for PowerShell fixes with dedicated reviewers vs. 31% for intent fixes with distributed review
committed diffs accelerated sharply after the agentic rollout (Q2 2025), with Android exhibiting the fastest growth, rising from near zero to approximately 1,500 diffs by September 2025.
